summary: Add two exact relay lemmas: strict first-switch monotonicity in the initial slope and a rigorous second-switch event-order obstruction near the equal-material limit; universal multiphase O3a remains open.

node.title: The first relay switch is strictly increasing in the initial slope
node.statement: For every mu>1 and q>1, the first crossing of S=U^2-mu^2V^2 in the initial max or min material cell is unique and its time tau_1(q) is C^1 and strictly increasing in q; the exact derivative is given by the implicit sine equation in the proof package.

node.title: Exact first-switch monotonicity
node.statement: In the complete relay model, restricted to the q>1 initial-slope chamber, the first switching time is uniquely defined and strictly increasing in q for both saturation signs after the initial-material time rescaling.

node.title: Successive relay event times have no global q-order
node.statement: There exist mu>1 and genuine contrasts R>1 arbitrarily close to one for which the second relay switching time is not nondecreasing in q>1; the proof uses the exact mu=3/2 equal-material limit and transverse event-time continuation.

node.title: Exact obstruction to event-by-event relay monotonicity
node.statement: The second switching time cannot be globally ordered by the initial slope q across all finite contrasts: for mu=3/2 and some R>1 arbitrarily close to one, there are q_a,q_b>1 with q_a<q_b but tau_2(q_b;R)<tau_2(q_a;R). This is an obstruction to a naive event-time induction only and is not a self-consistent O3a counterexample.

rationale.scope: The two additions are exact auxiliary relay lemmas. They deliberately do not claim universal relay injectivity, Jacobian nonsingularity, reflection rigidity, or a self-consistent counterexample.
rationale.route_value: The first lemma supplies the only unconditional q-order available at the first crossing. The second lemma proves that an induction using only successive event times cannot be the missing global injectivity proof; an augmented twist/action or Schur-complement invariant is required.
rationale.status_calibration: Both inferences are marked proved because the proof package uses exact trigonometric formulas, an explicit asymptotic limit, and transverse implicit-function continuation. The universal O3a frontier remains open in the canonical graph.

math_premise_contracts.scope: Finite positive contrasts and integer mode indices in the canonical weighted-string model.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The auxiliary relay parameters are chosen inside the canonical finite-contrast domain; the R=1 system appears only as a continuity limit and is not promoted as a target instance.

math_premise_contracts.scope: Positive bounded weighted Dirichlet strings and adjacent modes.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The transfer formulas and relay notation are exactly the canonical two-frequency scaling of this model.

math_premise_contracts.scope: Max/min relay signs, q>1 initial chamber, and effective switching events.
math_premise_contracts.contract_explanation: The proposition is explicitly weaker than self-consistency: terminal phases and equal integrals are not imposed on the comparison trajectories.

ordered_steps: On the initial material cell solve the two constant-coefficient IVPs explicitly and reduce S=0 to sin(y)=q sin(mu y) with 0<y<pi/mu.
Use strict decrease of sin(mu y)/sin(y), obtained from strict decrease of z cot z on (0,pi), to prove existence and uniqueness of the first root.
Differentiate the root equation and use the same cotangent inequality to prove the displayed derivative is strictly positive.
For the min relay rescale time by sqrt(R); the identical argument applies with the initial material frequency in place of one.
boundary_cases: mu>1 and q>1 are retained; the endpoint q=1 is not needed for this lemma.
The first event lies before the first V zero, so no phase wrapping or cell-boundary ambiguity occurs.
The statement is local to the initial cell and makes no terminal or symmetry assumption.

ordered_steps: At the equal-material comparison R=1 and mu=3/2, solve the q=1 event equations exactly to obtain the first two crossings 2pi/5 and 4pi/5, with the second crossing transverse.

Let q tend to infinity. The exact first-cell root tends to pi/mu, the post-first-event V slope is order -q, and the next crossing occurs after an O(1/q) increment; hence tau_2(q;1) tends to pi/mu=2pi/3.
Since 2pi/3<4pi/5, choose a finite Q with a strict separation from the q=1 second-event value.

Apply the implicit-function theorem at the transverse first two crossings and continuity in the post-first material R to transfer the strict separation to some genuine R>1 arbitrarily close to one and to q values strictly above one.
The min relay follows by the initial-material time rescaling and the same R downarrow 1 continuity argument.
boundary_cases: R=1 is only a limiting comparison; the conclusion is asserted for finite R>1.
q=1 is only a boundary anchor; the final two comparison slopes are both q>1.
The trajectories do not satisfy terminal indexed phases or equal relay integrals, so no O3a counterexample is claimed.
The result blocks only event-by-event time ordering, not every possible augmented twist or degree invariant.
